# noised-rules

Programmable launches for [Noised](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised), the quantum security layer for Solana: the two byte formats creators publish, and the code every Noised program and client uses to check and run them.

- **PXR1 launch rules**: extra restrictions during the Launch Guard (at most 72 hours). The transfer hook evaluates them **last**, after every built-in allow (sells, the end of the guard, the batch, claims and other exemptions, zero amounts) and every built-in denial. A rule can only reject, so rules cannot block a sell, a claim or the batch, and after the guard they do nothing. The Noised hook also never applies them to holders' exits: a transfer whose top-level instruction is the Noised PQ vault or shield (only the built-in checks apply to it).
- **PXG1 autopilot graphs**: post-launch automation of a token's treasury (buy back and burn, burn, pay declared recipients). Each node has a trigger, an optional condition, a per-run cap, a budget per epoch and a run limit per epoch.

Both share one condition mini-VM: a postfix array of 10-byte nodes over a boolean stack of at most 16 values.

The crate is `no_std`, has no `unsafe`, never allocates on the verify/evaluate paths, never recurses, and its library code is checked by clippy for panic freedom (`indexing_slicing`, `arithmetic_side_effects`, `unwrap_used`, `panic`, lossy casts: all denied). Every verifier returns a precise `Error` for any input; evaluation of a verified program cannot fail.

> **Status: pre-audit; 0.1.0 is on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/noised-rules).** No independent audit has been completed; the crate has had internal reviews by AI agents (review 4 and audit round 4, [docs/AUDIT.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/AUDIT.md)), mutation testing and a differential run against the TypeScript SDK. Byte formats are version 1 and frozen once a program using them is finalized; the parity vectors pin them. The programs that use this crate are deployed on Solana devnet only (upgradeable).

**Who uses it.** The Noised hook (`noised_hook`) verifies a launch's rules when its policy is created and evaluates them on every guarded transfer; the launchpad (`noised_launchpad`) verifies rules in `publish_rules` and hashes them for the attestation; the autopilot (`noised_autopilot`) verifies graphs in `publish_graph` and schedules and bounds every `run`. The TypeScript SDK (`@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable`) mirrors the formats, the verifiers and the evaluators byte for byte, tested against this crate's vectors. This README is normative for both byte formats ([docs/SPEC.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md) §1.9 and §9.2 refer to it).

## Install

Once it is on crates.io:

```sh
cargo add noised-rules                                   # parse, verify, evaluate: what an on-chain program needs
cargo add noised-rules --features alloc,sha2-backend     # clients and tools: owned programs, encoders, SHA-256
```

Or from this repository (pin a commit you reviewed):

```toml
[dependencies]
noised-rules = { git = "https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised", rev = "<commit>" }
# clients and tools: features = ["alloc", "sha2-backend"]
```

Version 0.1.0 was published by hand; later releases are published from this repository's release workflow. The published crate contains the library only (`src/`, this README, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`); the parity vectors shared with the SDK and the mutation check live in the repository.

## Features

| Feature | Adds |
|---|---|
| (none) | Parsing, verification, evaluation, due-ness, hashes over a `Sha256` trait. What an on-chain program needs. |
| `alloc` | `RulesProgram` / `GraphProgram`: owned programs with `encode()` / `decode()`, for clients, tools and tests. |
| `std` | Same as `alloc` (the error types implement `core::error::Error` without it). |
| `sha2-backend` | `Sha2`, a SHA-256 backend on the `sha2` crate. |

The only dependency is `sha2` 0.10 (optional, without default features).

### `no_std` notes

- `#![no_std]`, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Without `alloc` the crate never allocates: `RuleSet` and `Graph` borrow the input bytes, and every evaluation is a single pass over a fixed 16-value stack, with no recursion.
- The library code is linted for panic freedom (no indexing, no unchecked arithmetic, no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`, no lossy casts), and seeded property tests feed it arbitrary and mutated bytes.
- No clock and no randomness: the caller passes the time (`now_rel` for rules, `now` for graphs) and every balance.
- SHA-256 is the caller's (`Sha256` trait), so nothing is pulled into an on-chain program unless `sha2-backend` is enabled.

## Use

Every example in this section was compiled and run against this crate's source (features `alloc` and `sha2-backend`).

### Build, verify and evaluate a rule set

The rule the Noised devnet run used ("for the whole guard, deny a wallet-to-wallet transfer of more than 1,000 tokens"), built with the owned encoder, verified as the programs verify it, and evaluated as the hook evaluates it:

```rust
use noised_rules::rules::effect;
use noised_rules::{op, rules_hash, Node, Rule, RuleSet, RulesProgram, Sha2, TransferCtx, Violation};

let guard_secs: u32 = 30 * 60; // this launch's guard: 30 minutes
let thousand_tokens: u64 = 1_000 * 1_000_000; // 6 decimals

// The condition is a postfix program: IS_P2P, AMOUNT_GT(1,000 tokens), AND.
let program = RulesProgram {
    keys: vec![],
    rules: vec![Rule { from_rel: 0, to_rel: guard_secs, cond_off: 0, cond_len: 3, effect: effect::DENY, code: 7, arg: 0 }],
    nodes: vec![
        Node::new(op::rules::IS_P2P, 0, 0),
        Node::new(op::rules::AMOUNT_GT, 0, thousand_tokens),
        Node::new(op::AND, 0, 0),
    ],
};
let bytes = program.encode().expect("counts fit one byte");
assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 12 + 20 + 3 * 10); // 62 bytes

// What publish_rules and the hook's create_policy run: full verification, for this guard.
let set = RuleSet::verify(&bytes, guard_secs).expect("valid PXR1");
let hash: [u8; 32] = rules_hash::<Sha2>(&bytes); // SHA256("PHX-RULES-V1" || bytes): what the attestation signs

// What the hook runs on every transfer that reaches the rules step.
let p2p = |amount: u64| TransferCtx { now_rel: 60, is_p2p: true, amount, supply: 1_000_000_000_000_000, ..TransferCtx::default() };
assert_eq!(set.evaluate(&p2p(2_000 * 1_000_000)), Err(Violation { rule: 0, code: 7 }));
assert_eq!(set.evaluate(&p2p(500 * 1_000_000)), Ok(()));
// A buy is not wallet-to-wallet, and after the guard no rule is active.
let buy = TransferCtx { now_rel: 60, is_buy: true, amount: 2_000 * 1_000_000, ..TransferCtx::default() };
assert_eq!(set.evaluate(&buy), Ok(()));
assert_eq!(set.evaluate(&TransferCtx { now_rel: i64::from(guard_secs), ..p2p(2_000 * 1_000_000) }), Ok(()));

// A rule set whose window outlasts the guard is refused, with one precise error.
assert_eq!(RuleSet::verify(&bytes, 60).unwrap_err().name(), "WindowPastGuard");

// Stored bytes are re-read per transfer with the O(1) layout check only.
assert!(RuleSet::parse(&bytes).is_ok());
assert_eq!(RulesProgram::decode(&bytes).unwrap(), program);
```

Creators normally write rules with the SDK's builder or text grammar (`@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable`: `rules()`, `parseRules`, `compileRules`, `explainRules`), which produce exactly these bytes.

### Build, verify and schedule a graph

A daily buyback-and-burn, the shape of the Quick launch's Autopilot graph:

```rust
use noised_rules::graph::{action, trigger};
use noised_rules::{graph_hash, op, GNode, Graph, GraphCtx, GraphProgram, Node, NodeState, NotDue, Sha2};

const DAY: u32 = 86_400;
const SOL: u64 = 1_000_000_000;

// "Every day, once the pool has graduated and the treasury holds at least 0.5 SOL:
//  buy back and burn with at most 0.01 SOL, paying at most 3% over the reference price."
let program = GraphProgram {
    flags: 0,            // no operator
    operator: [0; 32],
    recipients: vec![],  // no DISTRIBUTE_SOL node, so no recipients
    nodes: vec![GNode {
        trigger: trigger::EVERY,
        trigger_arg: u64::from(DAY),
        cond_off: 0,
        cond_len: 3,
        action: action::BUYBACK_BURN,
        operator_gated: 0,
        epoch_secs: DAY,
        budget_per_epoch: SOL / 100,
        p1: SOL / 100, // max lamports in per run
        p2: 300,       // max premium over the reference price, bps
        max_runs_per_epoch: 1,
        reserved: [0; 5],
    }],
    cond: vec![
        Node::new(op::graph::GRADUATED, 0, 0),
        Node::new(op::graph::TREASURY_SOL_GTE, 0, SOL / 2),
        Node::new(op::AND, 0, 0),
    ],
};
let bytes = program.encode().expect("counts fit one byte");
assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 44 + 48 + 3 * 10); // 122 bytes

let graph = Graph::verify(&bytes).expect("valid PXG1");
let hash: [u8; 32] = graph_hash::<Sha2>(&bytes); // SHA256("PHX-GRAPH-V1" || bytes): the GraphRecord's address seed

// The autopilot program keeps one NodeState per node. A node that never ran is due at once.
let now: i64 = 1_800_000_000;
let mut states = [NodeState::default()];
let ctx = |now: i64, treasury_sol: u64, states: &[NodeState]| GraphCtx {
    now,
    treasury_sol,
    graduated: true,
    runs_in_epoch: graph.runs_in_epoch(states, now),
    ..GraphCtx::default()
};
assert_eq!(graph.runnable(0, &states, &ctx(now, SOL, &states)), Ok(()));
assert_eq!(graph.run_cap(0, &states[0], now), SOL / 100);
// Not enough SOL in the treasury: the condition is false.
assert_eq!(graph.runnable(0, &states, &ctx(now, SOL / 10, &states)), Err(NotDue::ConditionFalse));

// After a run, the next one waits a day.
states[0] = NodeState { last_run: now, last_seq: 1, epoch_start: now, runs_in_epoch: 1, spent_in_epoch: SOL / 100 };
assert_eq!(graph.due(0, &states, now + 3_600, true), Err(NotDue::Waiting));
assert_eq!(graph.due(0, &states, now + i64::from(DAY), true), Ok(()));
```

The real autopilot adds what this crate does not decide: the reference price and the observations behind the buyback's price bound, partial buybacks, tips, the 72-hour timelock on graph changes and the post-quantum authorizations ([SPEC §9](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md#9-autopilot-program-noised_autopilot)).

### On-chain

```rust
use noised_rules::{rules_hash, RuleSet, Sha256, TransferCtx};

struct SolSha256;
impl Sha256 for SolSha256 {
    fn hashv(parts: &[&[u8]]) -> [u8; 32] {
        solana_sha256_hasher::hashv(parts).to_bytes()
    }
}

// When the rules are published / the policy is created: full verification.
let set = RuleSet::verify(&bytes, guard_secs)?;           // Err(noised_rules::Error)
let hash = rules_hash::<SolSha256>(&bytes);               // SHA256("PHX-RULES-V1" || bytes)

// On every transfer (bytes stored after verification): layout check only, O(1).
let set = RuleSet::parse(&stored)?;
set.evaluate(&TransferCtx { now_rel, is_buy, is_p2p, amount, dest_balance_after, supply,
                            dest_owner, src_owner, top_program, tx_ix_count })?; // Err(Violation { rule, code })
```

`RuleSet::uses_leaf(op::rules::TOP_PROGRAM_IN | TX_IX_COUNT_GT)` tells the hook whether it needs the instructions sysvar at all.

For graphs: `Graph::verify(&bytes)`, `graph_hash`, `Graph::condition(i, &GraphCtx)`, `Graph::due(i, &states, now, graduated)`, `Graph::runnable(i, &states, &ctx)`, `Graph::run_cap(i, &state, now)`, `Graph::runs_in_epoch(&states, now)`, `Graph::shares(amount)`, `current_epoch`, `after_acyclic`.

## PXR1: launch rules

All integers little-endian. The length must be exact.

```text
offset  size
0       4     magic "PXR1"
4       1     version = 1
5       1     n_keys   (0..=8)
6       1     n_rules  (1..=16)
7       1     n_nodes  (0..=64)
8       4     reserved, zero
12      32*n_keys    keys
...     20*n_rules   rules
...     10*n_nodes   condition nodes
```

Maximum 12 + 8·32 + 16·20 + 64·10 = **1,228 bytes**.

Rule (20 bytes): `from_rel u32 | to_rel u32 | cond_off u8 | cond_len u8 | effect u8 | code u8 | arg u64`.

- Active while `from_rel <= now_rel < to_rel`, `now_rel` = seconds since the guard started (launch open time). Windows satisfy `from_rel < to_rel <= min(guard_secs, 259_200)`.
- Effects: `1 DENY` (reject if the condition holds; `arg` must be 0), `2 CAP_AMOUNT` (if the condition holds, reject when `amount > cap`), `3 CAP_DEST_BALANCE` (if the condition holds, reject when the destination balance after the transfer `> cap`).
- Caps: `arg > 0`, or with bit 63 set, `bps = arg & 0xFFFF` of the current supply, `1 <= bps <= 10_000`, bits 16..=62 zero; the cap is `floor(supply * bps / 10_000)`.
- `code` (0..=63) is shown to users and logged. The evaluator returns `Violation { rule: index, code }` for the first active rule that rejects.

Rule leaf predicates (`a` and `arg` not listed must be 0):

| op | name | operands | true when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x10 | IS_BUY | | the source is the pool's base vault |
| 0x11 | IS_P2P | | neither side is the pool or the protocol |
| 0x12 | TIME_LT | `arg <= guard` (s) | `now_rel < arg` |
| 0x13 | TIME_GE | `arg <= guard` (s) | `now_rel >= arg` |
| 0x14 | AMOUNT_GT | `arg` amount or bps (as caps; 0 allowed) | `amount > threshold` |
| 0x15 | DEST_BAL_AFTER_GT | `arg` as above | `dest_balance_after > threshold` |
| 0x16 | DEST_OWNER_IN | `a` = key mask | the destination owner is a key in the mask |
| 0x17 | SRC_OWNER_IN | `a` = key mask | the source owner is a key in the mask |
| 0x18 | TOP_PROGRAM_IN | `a` = key mask | the current top-level instruction's program is a key in the mask |
| 0x19 | TX_IX_COUNT_GT | `arg` | the transaction has more than `arg` top-level instructions |

A key mask is non-zero and names only existing keys (bit i = key i). A negative `now_rel` is before every bound.

`rules_hash = SHA256("PHX-RULES-V1" || bytes)`; all zeros means "no custom rules".

Canonical form (on top of the limits): keys are non-zero, distinct and each used by some mask; rule `i`'s condition starts where rule `i-1`'s ended (rule 0's at 0) and the last ends at `n_nodes`, so conditions partition the nodes in rule order and a transfer evaluates each node at most once; unused operands are zero.

## PXG1: autopilot graphs

```text
offset  size
0       4     magic "PXG1"
4       1     version = 1
5       1     n_recipients (0..=8)
6       1     n_nodes      (1..=16)
7       1     n_cond       (0..=96)
8       1     flags (bit 0: has operator; other bits zero)
9       3     reserved, zero
12      32    operator (zero iff no operator)
44      34*n_recipients   recipients: key [32] | bps u16
...     48*n_nodes        graph nodes
...     10*n_cond         condition nodes
```

Maximum 44 + 8·34 + 16·48 + 96·10 = **2,044 bytes**.

Graph node (48 bytes): `trigger u8 | trigger_arg u64 | cond_off u8 | cond_len u8 | action u8 | operator_gated u8 | epoch_secs u32 | budget_per_epoch u64 | p1 u64 | p2 u64 | max_runs_per_epoch u16 | reserved [0; 5]`.

| trigger | `trigger_arg` | due when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 EVERY | seconds, `>= 600` | `now >= last_run + trigger_arg` (exact; `last_run = 0` before the first run) |
| 2 AFTER | a node index `!= self`, in range; no cycles | the parent succeeded since this node's last run: `parent.last_seq > self.last_seq` |
| 3 ON_GRADUATED | 0 | graduated and never ran (`last_seq == 0`) |
| 4 WHEN | 0 (a condition is required) | always (the condition decides) |

| action | `p1` (> 0) | `p2` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 BUYBACK_BURN | max lamports in per run | max premium over the reference price, bps, `<= 2_000` |
| 2 BURN | max tokens per run | 0 |
| 3 DISTRIBUTE_SOL | max lamports per run (needs recipients) | 0 |
| 4, 5 | reserved for a later version: refused | |

`epoch_secs >= 3_600`, `budget_per_epoch > 0`, `max_runs_per_epoch >= 1`, `operator_gated` is 0 or 1 (1 needs an operator).

Graph leaf predicates (`a` and `arg` not listed must be 0):

| op | name | operands | true when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x20 | TREASURY_SOL_GTE | `arg` lamports | treasury wSOL `>= arg` |
| 0x21 | TREASURY_TOKEN_GTE | `arg` | treasury tokens `>= arg` |
| 0x22 | GRADUATED | | the pool migrated |
| 0x23 | PRICE_LTE | `arg` (sqrt price Q64.64) | sqrt price `<= arg` (over a range: its highest price) |
| 0x24 | PRICE_GTE | `arg` | sqrt price `>= arg` (over a range: its lowest price) |
| 0x25 | TIME_GE | `arg <= i64::MAX` (unix) | `now >= arg` |
| 0x26 | TIME_LT | `arg <= i64::MAX` | `now < arg` |
| 0x27 | RUNS_IN_EPOCH_LT | `a` = node index (in range), `arg` | node `a`'s runs in its current epoch `< arg` |

`Graph::condition` / `Graph::runnable` read one price, `GraphCtx::sqrt_price`, which must be the autopilot's slow reference price, never the spot price (a caller can move spot within its own transaction). The autopilot decides with `Graph::condition_over` / `Graph::runnable_over` instead: a condition holds only if it holds for **every** price of a `PriceRange { low, high }` (from the lower of the reference and the lowest observed price to the higher of the reference and the highest). The evaluation is three-valued (Kleene): each price leaf is "true at every price of the range" or "true at some", AND and OR combine both, NOT swaps them, and the answer is the first. So `PRICE_GTE` is judged on `low`, `PRICE_LTE` on `high`, and under NOT the other end; a wider range can only turn a condition false, and a single price (`PriceRange::at(p)`) gives exactly `condition`. It is conservative, never permissive: a condition that holds at every single price but needs different leaves at different prices (`PRICE_GTE x OR NOT PRICE_GTE x`) is false over a range that straddles `x`.

`graph_hash = SHA256("PHX-GRAPH-V1" || bytes)`.

Canonical form: recipients non-zero, distinct, bps > 0 each, summing to exactly 10,000, and used by some DISTRIBUTE_SOL node; the operator key is set exactly when the flag is, and some node is operator-gated exactly when there is an operator; a node without a condition has `cond_off = 0`; otherwise conditions start where the previous non-empty one ended and the last ends at `n_cond`; reserved bytes zero.

### Run state

`NodeState { last_run, last_seq, epoch_start, runs_in_epoch, spent_in_epoch }`, kept by the autopilot program. `last_seq` is the autopilot's global sequence number of the node's last successful run (successful runs are numbered 1, 2, 3, ... across all nodes), so AFTER works even for runs in the same second.

Epochs (`current_epoch`): the stored epoch while `epoch_start <= now < epoch_start + epoch_secs` (or the clock is before `epoch_start`); otherwise a fresh one (0 runs, 0 spent) starting at `now - (now - epoch_start) % epoch_secs`, so epochs stay aligned to the first and callers cannot shift them by timing their runs.

`Graph::due` checks, in order: the trigger, `runs < max_runs_per_epoch` (`MaxRunsReached`), `spent < budget_per_epoch` (`BudgetSpent`). `Graph::runnable` then checks the condition (`ConditionFalse`). `run_cap = min(p1, budget - spent)`. `shares(amount)[i] = floor(amount * bps_i / 10_000)`; the dust stays in the treasury.

## Integration notes

Transfer hook ([SPEC §1.9](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md#19-creator-launch-rules-and-the-hook-policy), [HOOKS.md §2](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/HOOKS.md#2-launch-guard-rules)):

- Verify once with `RuleSet::verify(bytes, guard_secs)` when the policy is created (`InvalidRules` on error) and store the bytes; per transfer use `RuleSet::parse` (O(1)) and `evaluate`.
- Call `evaluate` last: after the sell check, `now >= guard_end`, the snipe shield, zero amounts, exempt owners (claims, escrow), the batch and the built-in denials; the Noised hook skips it for holders' exits (top-level program = the Noised vault or shield). At that point a transfer is a buy (`is_buy`, source = base vault) or wallet to wallet (`is_p2p = !is_buy`: sells and protocol accounts returned earlier). `tests/model.rs` is this pipeline as a model.
- `now_rel = now - launch_ts` (negative is fine: nothing is active). `supply` is the mint's current supply. `top_program` is the program id of `load_instruction_at(load_current_index())`; `tx_ix_count` is the sysvar's instruction count. The Noised hook reads the sysvar and the supply only for a transfer that reaches this step, whatever leaves the rules use (it needs `top_program` for the exits, and bps caps need the supply).
- On `Err(Violation { rule, code })`, log both and fail with `RuleDenied`. `code == CODE_MALFORMED` (255) can only come from bytes that were never verified.

Autopilot ([SPEC §9](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md#9-autopilot-program-noised_autopilot)): keep a `NodeState` per node and a global run counter for `last_seq`; build `GraphCtx` with the reference (EMA) sqrt price and `runs_in_epoch = graph.runs_in_epoch(&states, now)`; `runnable` decides whether `run` may proceed and `run_cap` bounds the amount. A node that never ran has `last_run = 0`, so an EVERY node is due at once; set `last_run` at activation to delay its first run by one period.

## Cost (SBPF v3, measured)

Measured with a probe program built by `cargo-build-sbf --arch v3` (platform-tools v1.57) and run in LiteSVM 0.17: `sol_log_compute_units` before and after each call, the two syscalls subtracted.

| Path | CU |
|---|---|
| `RuleSet::parse`, 1,228 bytes | 40 |
| `parse` + `evaluate`: 8 keys, 16 active DENY rules, 64 nodes, every condition evaluated, none rejects | 3,855 |
| `parse` + `evaluate`: 16 active bps CAP rules all over their caps, 32 bps leaves, every condition evaluated | 6,078 |
| `parse` + `evaluate`: the first rule rejects | 460 |
| `RuleSet::verify`, 1,228 bytes | 4,471 |
| `Graph::verify`, 2,044 bytes | 5,655 |
| `Graph::parse` + `runnable` for all 16 nodes of the largest graph (default states: 5 conditions evaluated, the AFTER nodes stop at their trigger) | 2,045 |
| `Graph::parse` + `runnable` of one WHEN node with the longest condition (96 nodes, all evaluated): the per-run worst case | 2,592 |
| `Graph::verify`, one node with a 96-node condition | 3,567 |
| `Graph::parse` + `shares` (8 recipients, 128-bit split) + `run_cap` for 16 nodes + `runs_in_epoch` | 2,667 |

Figures move by up to a few hundred CU between builds of the probe (inlining and code layout); the margins below do not depend on that. The per-transfer worst case stays under half of the spec's 15k budget; conditions partition the nodes, so no rule set can make a transfer evaluate more than 64 nodes. A graph run evaluates one node's condition, at most 96 nodes. Basis-point thresholds are computed in `u64` (`q * bps + floor(r * bps / 10_000)` with `supply = q * 10_000 + r`), which measured cheaper than a 128-bit multiply. The hook's own number (sysvar reads included) belongs in its LiteSVM suite.

## The condition VM

Node: `op u8 | a u8 | arg u64`. `0x00 TRUE`, `0x01 FALSE` push; `0x02 AND`, `0x03 OR` pop two, push one; `0x04 NOT` pops one, pushes one; leaves push one. All of `TRUE..NOT` take no operands. Verification per node, in order: the operation is known in the context (rules leaves are unknown in graphs and vice versa: `UnknownOp`), operands (`NonZeroOperand`, `BadKeyMask`, `BadBps`, `TimeOutOfRange`, `BadNodeRef`), then the stack: `StackUnderflow`, `StackOverflow` (more than 16 values), and at the end exactly one value (`LeftoverValues`).

## Verification order

The first failing check wins, so every input maps to one error name (`Error::name()`, the parity contract).

PXR1 (`RuleSet::verify(bytes, guard_secs)`):

1. Layout (`RuleSet::parse`): `TooShort` (< 12 bytes), `BadMagic`, `BadVersion`, `ReservedNonZero`, `TooManyKeys`, `NoRules`, `TooManyRules`, `TooManyNodes`, `BadLength`.
2. Each key in order: `ZeroKey`, `DuplicateKey`.
3. Each rule in order: `BadWindow`, `WindowPastGuard`, `BadCode`, effect (`UnknownEffect`; DENY `DenyArgNonZero`; CAP `BadBps` / `ZeroCap`), `EmptyCondition`, `ConditionNotContiguous`, `ConditionOutOfRange`, then the condition's nodes (VM order above).
4. `UnreferencedNode`, then `UnusedKey`.

PXG1 (`Graph::verify(bytes)`):

1. Layout (`Graph::parse`): `TooShort` (< 44 bytes), `BadMagic`, `BadVersion`, `UnknownFlags`, `ReservedNonZero`, `TooManyRecipients`, `NoGraphNodes`, `TooManyGraphNodes`, `TooManyNodes`, `BadLength`.
2. `MissingOperator` (flag, zero key), `UnexpectedOperator` (key, no flag).
3. Each recipient: `ZeroRecipient`, `DuplicateRecipient`, `ZeroRecipientBps`; then `BadRecipientBps` (sum != 10,000, computed without overflow).
4. Each node in order: `ReservedNonZero`; trigger (`UnknownTrigger`, `EveryTooShort`, `BadAfterRef`, `AfterCycle` for itself, `TriggerArgNonZero`, `WhenWithoutCondition`); action (`ReservedAction`, `UnknownAction`); `ZeroP1`; `PremiumTooHigh` (BUYBACK_BURN) / `P2NonZero` (others); `NoRecipients` (DISTRIBUTE_SOL); `BadOperatorGated`, `GatedWithoutOperator`; `EpochTooShort`; `ZeroBudget`; `ZeroMaxRuns`; condition (`ConditionNotContiguous`, `ConditionOutOfRange`, then its nodes).
5. `UnreferencedNode`, `AfterCycle`, `OperatorUnused`, `RecipientsUnused`.

## Parity vectors

`tests/vectors/rules.json` and `tests/vectors/graph.json` hold 46 valid rule sets with 736 evaluation cases and 41 valid graphs with 492 condition and schedule cases (hex, hash) and 72 invalid rule sets and 76 invalid graphs (hex and the expected error name: every error of each format appears), plus threshold and epoch cases. `u64`/`i64`/`u128` values are decimal strings, bytes are hex. The test `vectors` regenerates nothing by default: it rebuilds the vectors from `tests/common/cases.rs`, checks every expected result against an independent reference model, and fails if the files differ. After a deliberate change:

```sh
NOISED_REGEN_VECTORS=1 cargo test -p noised-rules --test vectors
```

(PowerShell: `$env:NOISED_REGEN_VECTORS='1'; cargo test -p noised-rules --test vectors`), then review the diff: any change to an existing entry is a format change.

### Differential run with the SDK

`tests/differential.rs` (format `DIFF1`) is a seeded generator mirrored line for line by the SDK's `test/programmable/differential.ts`: case `i` draws from SplitMix64 seeded with `seed + i`, builds a plausible rule set or graph with its own little-endian writer, then applies 0 to 3 byte or field mutations (header counts, windows, effects, caps, ops, operands, keys, recipients, triggers, actions, truncation, an extra node), so the run covers valid programs, almost every error ordering, and the unverified (parse-only) paths: fail-closed evaluation, thresholds of out-of-range bps, schedules with missing states, shares that overflow. `tests/vectors/differential.json` holds 3,000 cases per format, one entry each: `<len>:<FNV-1a 64 of the bytes> <verify> <parse> <FNV-1a 64 of the full result line>`. The full line holds the hash or error, the parser's verdict, the codec round trip, every evaluation and condition (rules), every `due` / `runnable` / condition / `run_cap` / `runs_in_epoch` (graphs, one index past the end included), the shares and the threshold samples. The file also lists `Error` and `NotDue` names in discriminant order. The SDK copies the file and must reproduce every entry. The test asserts that the cases reach every error of each format, every schedule outcome and the parse-only paths, and regenerates with the same `NOISED_REGEN_VECTORS=1` (`--test differential`).

```sh
NOISED_DIFF_DUMP=rules:17 cargo test -p noised-rules --test differential -- --nocapture   # one case in full (graph:N)
NOISED_DIFF_OUT=diff.json NOISED_DIFF_CASES=100000 cargo test -p noised-rules --test differential
# then in the SDK: NOISED_DIFF_FILE=diff.json vitest run test/programmable/differential.test.ts
```

## Tests

`cargo test -p noised-rules` (the crate dev-depends on itself with `alloc` and `sha2-backend`): unit tests for every check, leaf, effect, trigger and limit at its edges; an independent reference model (`tests/common`) the evaluators are compared with on random verified programs; seeded property tests (arbitrary and mutated bytes never panic, codecs round-trip, verification is deterministic); a model of the hook (`tests/model.rs`) showing rules only add restrictions and never see sells, claims, the batch or anything after the guard; the parity vectors and the differential run with the SDK (`tests/vectors.rs`, `tests/differential.rs`). `scripts/rules/rules_mutants.py` runs the mutation check.
